source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.34
text: Identifying and removing off-type and mixed-variety plants (ការកំណត់ពូជលាយ និងពូជផ្សេងគ្នា) is an ongoing task that must be carried out continuously from the nursery stage through tillering and up to harvest, not as a single one-time pass. Off-types are identified by comparing plants against the known reference characteristics of the registered variety, and are removed (rogued out) by hand as soon as spotted. Visual indicators used to spot off-types/contaminants include: a different plant height than the surrounding crop (too tall or too short); different leaf color or leaf angle; different panicle/grain color; flowering or heading noticeably earlier or later than the rest of the field; and the presence of weedy/wild rice (ស្រូវព្រៃ), typically recognizable by red-pericarp grain, awned grains, and grains that shatter easily.
